description: Create the internal compute-provider abstraction package at services/amazai/compute/ with the ComputeProvider enum, ComputeRequirements and ComputeAssignment dataclasses, the ComputeProvider Protocol/interface, the AgentCore provider adapter wrapping the existing amazai.agentcore.AgentCore, the EC2Desktop provider placeholder (interface only, no boto3 calls), and the pure compute routing policy. Includes a new tests/test_compute.py covering provider selection. This is the load-bearing feature and the foundation the rest of the phase and the next phase (DEV-01) build on. NOTE: this feature also serves as the environment-setup baseline step for this task since the venv already exists; the coder must run the full suite first to confirm the documented baseline before making changes.
steps: Confirm the environment: from /projects/sandbox/AmazAI, run '.venv/bin/python -m pytest --tb=no -q' and confirm the ONLY failures are the 3 pre-existing ones in tests/test_gaps_api.py (ResourceNotFoundException). If the venv is missing, recreate it: 'uv venv --python 3.11.15 .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements-dev.txt', then remove any .python-version file pyenv may have written.

Create the package services/amazai/compute/__init__.py. Give it 'from __future__ import annotations' and a substantial module docstring explaining WHY the compute abstraction exists (AgentCore stays the default ephemeral runtime; EC2 Desktop is a narrow optional escape hatch behind one interface), citing docs/architecture/04-workspaces.md and docs/architecture/05-run-lifecycle.md. Re-export the public names (ComputeProvider, ComputeRequirements, ComputeAssignment, ComputeProviderInterface/Protocol, AgentCoreProvider, EC2DesktopProvider, and the policy function) so callers import from amazai.compute. IMPORTANT naming guard: do NOT name any function parameter or local the same as a module it imports from amazai.* (tests/test_no_shadowed_modules.py enforces this across services/). Also avoid a top-level module filename that collides with an existing services module name.

In services/amazai/compute/types.py (or models.py within the package - but avoid shadowing the top-level amazai.models; prefer 'types.py'): define 'class ComputeProvider(str, Enum)' with members AGENTCORE = 'agentcore' and EC2_DESKTOP = 'ec2_desktop', following the (str, Enum) idiom from router.ToolPath / states.RunState. Define 'ComputeRequirements' as a frozen @dataclass of explicit boolean/needs flags that describe when a full computer is required: full_desktop: bool = False, persistent_dev_env: bool = False, os_level_app: bool = False, heavy_local_tooling: bool = False (names taken from the user instruction). Add a classmethod/factory 'from_run(run: dict) -> ComputeRequirements' and/or 'from_agent(agent: dict) -> ComputeRequirements' that reads an OPTIONAL nested dict (e.g. run.get('compute', {}).get('requirements') or agent.get('compute', {}).get('requirements')) and defaults every flag to False when absent - so existing records with no compute field resolve to all-False (=> AgentCore). Add a property like 'requires_full_computer' that is True iff any flag is set. Define 'ComputeAssignment' as a frozen @dataclass: provider: ComputeProvider, reason: str, and any fields the next phase needs to record the selection (e.g. requirements: ComputeRequirements). Provide a to_dict()/as_record() that produces the JSON-safe dict persisted on the run (e.g. {'provider': ..., 'reason': ...}).

In services/amazai/compute/policy.py: implement the pure routing policy mirroring router.select_path's STYLE - pure input (ComputeRequirements, plus optionally the run/agent dicts) -> frozen ComputeAssignment, no AWS calls, no store access. Function e.g. 'select_compute_provider(requirements: ComputeRequirements) -> ComputeAssignment' (and/or a convenience 'select_for_run(run, agent) -> ComputeAssignment' that builds requirements then delegates). Rule: return EC2_DESKTOP only when requirements.requires_full_computer is True (any of full_desktop/persistent_dev_env/os_level_app/heavy_local_tooling); otherwise AGENTCORE. The reason string must name why (e.g. 'no full-computer requirement; default AgentCore' or 'requires persistent developer environment'). Keep the default the safe path so absent/backward-compat records get AgentCore.

In services/amazai/compute/base.py: define the provider interface as a typing.Protocol named ComputeProviderInterface (or an abstract base) declaring the lifecycle contract every provider must satisfy. Model it on the run lifecycle hooks the user asked for: acquire(run, agent, *, store) -> handle/context, wait_until_ready(...) -> readiness, execute(...) , release(...). Give each method a docstring. Include a 'provider' attribute/property returning the ComputeProvider enum value. The interface must be provider-agnostic so both adapters implement it.

In services/amazai/compute/agentcore_provider.py: implement AgentCoreProvider that ADAPTS the existing amazai.agentcore.AgentCore (import it; construct/accept one via __init__ so it stays testable without AWS - accept an injected AgentCore like AgentCore.__init__ accepts runtime=/control=). Its provider property returns ComputeProvider.AGENTCORE. acquire/wait_until_ready are effectively no-ops for AgentCore (the microVM/session is acquired implicitly by invoke) - document that acquire returns immediately-ready because AgentCore sessions are ephemeral and managed by the runtime; wait_until_ready returns ready True. execute delegates to the wrapped AgentCore's invoke_stream(...) and/or exec(...) WITHOUT reimplementing them (do NOT modify agentcore.py). release is a no-op / documents that session teardown is handled by AgentCore's 14-day TTL and the existing sync-at-run-end. The point: existing AgentCore behavior is unchanged; this is a thin passthrough so the same lifecycle shape covers both providers.

In services/amazai/compute/ec2_provider.py: implement EC2DesktopProvider as a PLACEHOLDER that defines the interface sufficiently for the NEXT phase to implement, WITHOUT provisioning EC2 (no live boto3 EC2/SSM calls). Its provider property returns ComputeProvider.EC2_DESKTOP. Define clearly-named methods matching the sequence the user listed, each with a docstring describing intended behavior and each raising NotImplementedError (mirror agentcore.update_filesystem's NotImplementedError style) or returning a typed 'not yet provisioned' placeholder: dedicated machine lookup (e.g. lookup_dedicated_instance), instance start (start_instance), Systems Manager readiness (wait_for_ssm_ready), workspace restoration (restore_workspace), command/action execution (execute / run_command), workspace persistence (persist_workspace), instance stop (stop_instance). Map these onto the acquire->wait_until_ready->execute->release lifecycle from base.py (e.g. acquire = lookup + start; wait_until_ready = SSM readiness; execute = run_command; release = persist_workspace + stop_instance). Docstrings MUST state that EC2 actions will flow through the SAME approvals, evidence, secrets, and audit systems as AgentCore (reuse, do not fork) and that workspace persistence aligns with the S3-versioned-drive-as-system-of-record model in docs/architecture/04-workspaces.md.

Add a small provider registry/factory in the package (e.g. in __init__.py or a providers.py): 'get_provider(provider: ComputeProvider, **deps) -> ComputeProviderInterface' returning AgentCoreProvider for AGENTCORE and EC2DesktopProvider for EC2_DESKTOP, so the orchestrator can go from a ComputeAssignment to a live provider object in one call.

Create tests/test_compute.py following the pytest STYLE of tests/test_router.py (plain test functions/classes, no heavy fixtures needed for the pure policy). Cover: (a) an empty/default run (no 'compute' field) selects AGENTCORE; (b) an agent/run with no compute field selects AGENTCORE (backward-compat); (c) each of full_desktop / persistent_dev_env / os_level_app / heavy_local_tooling set individually selects EC2_DESKTOP; (d) requires_full_computer is False for default and True when any flag set; (e) the ComputeAssignment reason names why; (f) get_provider returns the right provider type and provider.provider matches the enum; (g) AgentCoreProvider can be constructed with an injected fake AgentCore and its execute delegates to the wrapped object's invoke_stream/exec (assert delegation via a fake, do NOT call real AWS); (h) EC2DesktopProvider placeholder methods raise NotImplementedError (or return the documented placeholder) - assert they do not perform provisioning. Keep everything pure/mocked - no real boto3.

Run '.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_compute.py -q' and confirm all new tests pass. Then run the full suite '.venv/bin/python -m pytest --tb=short -q' and confirm no NEW failures beyond the 3 pre-existing test_gaps_api.py failures, and that tests/test_no_shadowed_modules.py passes.
acceptance_criteria: services/amazai/compute/ package exists and 'from amazai import compute' plus 'from amazai.compute import ComputeProvider, ComputeRequirements, ComputeAssignment, AgentCoreProvider, EC2DesktopProvider' import without error.
ComputeProvider is a (str, Enum) with members agentcore and ec2_desktop.

select_compute_provider (or select_for_run) returns AGENTCORE for a run/agent with no compute field and for all-False requirements; returns EC2_DESKTOP only when at least one full-computer flag is set.
AgentCoreProvider wraps the existing amazai.agentcore.AgentCore without modifying agentcore.py and delegates execution to its invoke_stream/exec.

EC2DesktopProvider defines the full lifecycle interface (dedicated machine lookup, instance start, SSM readiness, workspace restoration, command execution, workspace persistence, instance stop) and performs NO EC2 provisioning (methods raise NotImplementedError or return documented placeholders).
tests/test_compute.py exists, follows tests/test_router.py style, and passes.
Running '.venv/bin/python -m pytest' shows no NEW failures beyond the 3 documented pre-existing test_gaps_api.py failures; tests/test_no_shadowed_modules.py passes.
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/AmazAI && .venv/bin/python -m pytest --tb=short -q  (expect only the 3 pre-existing test_gaps_api.py failures)
findings: Baseline confirmed before changes: full suite green except the 3 documented pre-existing tests/test_gaps_api.py failures (ResourceNotFoundException on PutItem, environmental moto/table issue). No .python-version file present. Created services/amazai/compute/ with types.py (ComputeProvider(str,Enum), frozen ComputeRequirements with from_run/from_agent + requires_full_computer, frozen ComputeAssignment with as_record/to_dict), policy.py (pure select_compute_provider + select_for_run mirroring router.select_path; EC2 only when requires_full_computer, else AgentCore, reason string names why), base.py (ComputeProviderInterface typing.Protocol, runtime_checkable, acquire/wait_until_ready/execute/release + provider property), agentcore_provider.py (AgentCoreProvider adapts injected amazai.agentcore.AgentCore; acquire/wait_until_ready/release are documented no-ops, execute delegates to invoke_stream/exec; agentcore.py untouched), ec2_provider.py (EC2DesktopProvider placeholder; granular lookup/start/SSM/restore/run_command/persist/stop + base lifecycle all raise NotImplementedError; docstrings state reuse of same approvals/evidence/secrets/audit and S3-versioned-drive alignment; no boto3), and __init__.py (re-exports + get_provider factory). Package name types.py chosen to avoid shadowing amazai.models. Verification: tests/test_compute.py (43 new tests) passes; tests/test_no_shadowed_modules.py passes; full suite shows only the same 3 pre-existing test_gaps_api.py failures (no regressions). NOTE: tracked __pycache__/*.pyc files (committed despite being gitignored) show as modified after running tests; these are incidental build artifacts and were intentionally NOT staged.
